terms.definition: A waste product made in the liver from the breakdown of excess amino acids (deamination), removed by the kidneys in urine.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: deamination produces ammonia, which is converted to urea.

terms.definition: Blood is filtered in the kidney: water, glucose, ions and urea leave the blood.
terms.examiner: Large molecules such as proteins stay in the blood.

terms.definition: Useful substances such as all the glucose, some ions and as much water as the body needs are taken back into the blood.
Anti-diuretic hormone, released by the pituitary gland when the blood is too concentrated; it makes the kidney tubules more permeable so more water is reabsorbed.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. An example of negative feedback.

terms.definition: Treatment for kidney failure: blood passes over a partially permeable membrane next to dialysis fluid, so urea and excess ions diffuse out.
terms.examiner: The fluid has the same glucose and useful ion concentrations as normal blood, so these are not lost.

terms.definition: A healthy kidney from a donor replaces the failed kidney.
terms.examiner: Risk of rejection: the patient takes drugs to suppress the immune system.
